drawdown_context: MYGN is a molecular diagnostics company (hereditary cancer / MyRisk, prenatal / Foresight-Prequel, tumor profiling / MyChoice CDx, and pharmacogenomics / GeneSight). FY24 revenue $837.6M (+11%) with a $127.3M net loss; cash declined to $102.4M against a $115M ABL revolver that matures June 30, 2026 (inside the post-cutoff window). In Q4 2024 UnitedHealthcare announced it would stop covering multi-gene panel pharmacogenetic tests including GeneSight effective 1/1/2025 — eliminating ~$45M of FY24 revenue and triggering a $43.0M GeneSight intangible impairment plus a $12.4M EndoPredict divestiture loss. The CEO (Paul Diaz) announced his departure four days before the 10-K filed (2/24/2025 announcement, 2/28/2025 10-K) for an April 30, 2025 effective date. A qui tam False Claims Act case (Carolina Urology Partners kickback allegations) filed in 2022 was unsealed January 22, 2025 — and this is MYGN's second material FCA matter after settling the Crescendo Bioscience qui tam in 2022 for $48M. Stock at $4.25 on 5/15/2025 (down from low-$20s a year earlier).

rfm_tuples.R: [Pharmacogenomics revenue $170.2M for FY24, +23% YoY... in Q1 2025] Pharmacogenomics revenue decreased $7.9 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to the same period in the prior year due primarily to a 22% decrease in the average revenue per test. Pharmacogenomics revenue for the three months ended March 31, 2025 has been negatively impacted by UnitedHealthcare's recent change in coverage of the GeneSight test under its commercial, individual exchange benefit, and certain managed Medicaid plans.
rfm_tuples.f: Compare 10-K narrative ('we anticipate negative impact') to actual Q1 2025 10-Q realization. The 10-K quantifies $45.0M of UHC GeneSight revenue at risk but does NOT give a 2025 revenue guide; the Q1 10-Q (filed 5/7/2025, 8 days pre-cutoff) reveals the actual hit rate.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2025 10-Q (accession 0000899923-25-000048, filed 5/7/2025) Item 2 MD&A revenue table
rfm_tuples.M_value: Pharmacogenomics rev/test fell -22% in Q1 2025 vs Q1 2024 ($31.0M vs $38.9M total despite +2% volume). That is essentially the full UHC pricing hit landing in a single quarter. Annualized, this implies a ~$30-35M GeneSight revenue run-rate loss vs the $45M FY24 UHC concentration — consistent with the 10-K's risk disclosure but quantifies the cliff. Worse, the managed Medicaid step-down was only beginning in Q1 2025 ('expected during the first half of 2025'), so Q2 2025 should be incrementally worse.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: the 10-K's UHC risk disclosure was directionally correct but the Q1 10-Q confirms the speed and magnitude of the cliff. The Pharmacogenomics reporting unit had only a 43.6% fair-value cushion post-impairment, modeled at a 10.0% WACC — a -22% pricing miss in the very first quarter suggests management's DCF base case (and therefore the residual $43M of GeneSight intangibles + Pharmacogenomics goodwill) is already stale at the 10-Q date.

rfm_tuples.R: [FY24 Hereditary Cancer revenue +11% to $364.5M on 6% price + 5% volume — 'driving growth' narrative] vs [Q1 2025] Hereditary Cancer revenue decreased $1.8 million for the three months ended March 31, 2025 compared to the same period in the prior year due to a 5% decrease in average revenue per test, partially offset by a 3% increase in testing volume.
rfm_tuples.f: Hereditary Cancer is 44% of revenue and the historical core franchise. Test whether the 'price up + volume up' FY24 story extends into the post-cutoff window using the Q1 2025 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 7 MD&A revenue table + Q1 2025 10-Q Item 2 MD&A revenue table
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24: +6% price, +5% volume = +11% revenue ($327.8M -> $364.5M). Q1 2025: -5% price, +3% volume = -2% revenue ($88.1M -> $86.3M). The price-per-test direction flipped from +6% to -5% YoY in one quarter on the largest segment, which is NOT explained in the 10-Q ('decrease in average revenue per test' with no payor cited). Implies the FY24 price tailwind was not durable — likely catch-up collections / one-time payor coverage reclassifications, not contracted rate increases.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B (claim evolution between 10-K and pre-cutoff 10-Q). The FY24 10-K leans heavily on Hereditary Cancer growth to offset GeneSight, framing 11% growth as a structural tailwind. The Q1 10-Q reveals the price piece was not contractual — when it normalizes, revenue contracts. This is exactly the lying-by-omission pattern the framework targets: management knew (or should have known) the Q1 trend at the 2/28/2025 10-K filing date but framed the FY24 result as 'driving growth.' The Hereditary Cancer price reversal is, in dollars, larger than the entire GeneSight UHC impact and was not flagged.

rfm_tuples.R: We believe that our existing cash and cash equivalents of $102.4 million as of December 31, 2024, our expected cash flow from operations, and our availability to borrow will be sufficient to meet our anticipated cash requirements for at least the next 12 months. [...] availability under the ABL Facility was $56.0 million [...] The ABL Facility matures on June 30, 2026. [Required to maintain] a fixed charge coverage ratio of at least 1.0 to 1.0 if availability under the ABL Facility is less than the greater of (a) $10.6 million and (b) 12.5% of the lesser of the maximum commitment amount and the borrowing base.
rfm_tuples.f: Test runway under the actual Q1 2025 trajectory. FY24 operating cash use was $8.7M; FY23 was $110.9M. The 10-K projects a return to positive operating cash. The Q1 10-Q is the highest-discrimination pre-cutoff signal.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2025 10-Q Condensed Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows + ABL note
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2025: operating cash use $(16.3)M (vs $(18.6)M in Q1 2024); ABL outstanding balance grew from $39.6M (12/31/2024) to $59.3M (3/31/2025), +$19.7M draw in 90 days. Cash and equivalents fell from $102.4M to $91.8M. Availability under the ABL fell from $56.0M to $41.9M (-25% in one quarter). At the Q1 burn rate (cash use ~$10-11M/qtr plus debt service plus working-capital seasonality reversing), the remaining $41.9M of revolver headroom buys roughly 4-5 quarters BEFORE the 6/30/2026 maturity itself becomes the binding constraint. Management is compliant with covenants because availability is well above the 12.5% trigger ($10.6M floor), but the headroom is collapsing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the 10-K says 'sufficient for at least 12 months' (i.e., through 2/28/2026), which is also 4 months BEFORE the ABL matures 6/30/2026. The 10-K is technically truthful but uses the going-concern-look-forward framework to avoid disclosing that the refinance cliff and the runway cliff are the same event. Q1 confirms the trajectory — net cash position (cash - ABL) flipped from +$62.8M (12/31/24) to +$32.5M (3/31/25), a $30M swing in 90 days. Combine with the UHC revenue cliff and the Hereditary Cancer price reversal, and the 'sufficient for 12 months' disclosure becomes the type of claim where the framework can demonstrate the company is right about the letter and wrong about the substance.

rfm_tuples.R: On February 24, 2025, Paul J. Diaz, our President and Chief Executive Officer, announced that he will step down from those positions, and resign from our Board of Directors effective April 30, 2025, after which Mr. Diaz will continue to serve as a consultant for another year. [...] Our Board of Directors appointed Samraat S. Raha, our current Chief Operating Officer, to succeed Mr. Diaz as our President and Chief Executive Officer.
rfm_tuples.f: Time the CEO departure announcement (2/24/2025) against (a) the UHC GeneSight announcement (Q4 2024), (b) the qui tam unsealing (1/22/2025), and (c) the 10-K filing date (2/28/2025). The pattern of value-destroying disclosures preceding a CEO exit announcement four days before the 10-K is a textbook insider_vs_calendar signal.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors + Item 7 MD&A 'Business Updates' + Q1 2025 10-Q + 8-K filed 2/24/2025
rfm_tuples.M_value: Timeline: (i) ~Oct/Nov 2024 UHC announces GeneSight non-coverage during Q4 2024 (triggers $43M intangible impairment); (ii) 1/22/2025 qui tam complaint unsealed (a second False Claims Act case, after a $48M Crescendo Bioscience settlement in April 2022); (iii) 2/24/2025 CEO Diaz announces resignation effective 4/30/2025 — also resigns from Board, with a one-year consulting tail (a structure that preserves access to information but distances him from fiduciary signatures); (iv) 2/28/2025 10-K filed and signed by Diaz as CEO. New CEO Raha is a recent internal hire (COO since 12/2023, ~16 months as COO) — not an externally-recruited turnaround CEO. CCO (Chief Commercial Officer) is also being backfilled at the same time (Verratti -> COO, new CCO search underway).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the framework's strongest tell is when a CEO exits the same quarter as a goodwill impairment + a second FCA matter + an internal-only succession with a consulting tail. The 10-K acknowledges the change but does not frame it as a stress signal. The simultaneous CCO transition is the second-order tell — commercial leadership turning over while the largest payor (UHC) walks away is the kind of cluster that the framework flags.

rfm_tuples.R: On January 22, 2025, the U.S. District Court for the Western District of North Carolina unsealed a qui tam complaint, filed on November 3, 2022, against Carolina Urology Partners, PLLC, and certain of its current or former physician partners, and the Company and certain of its former employees, alleging violations of the False Claims Act. [...] On January 21, 2025, after a multi-year investigation into the Company's alleged conduct, the United States declined to intervene. [10-K says] The Company was not aware of the complaint until after it was unsealed and the Company has not been served the complaint yet.
rfm_tuples.f: Pattern-match the new FCA case against the prior 2022 Crescendo Bioscience FCA settlement to test for recidivism. Then confirm progression via the pre-cutoff Q1 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 12 Commitments and Contingencies + Q1 2025 10-Q Note 12 + EDGAR records of prior CBI qui tam
rfm_tuples.M_value: Prior FCA: April 1, 2022 settlement for $45.25M to US + State of California + $2.75M to relator's counsel = $48.0M total, related to Crescendo Bioscience (CBI) Vectra DA testing. New FCA: Carolina Urology Partners filed 11/3/2022 (under seal) — meaning the new FCA complaint was filed within 7 months of the CBI settlement. The DOJ investigated 'multi-year' (2023-2024) before declining to intervene on 1/21/2025. The complaint was served on the Company on 4/16/2025 per the Q1 2025 10-Q (a fact the 10-K could not yet disclose). Two FCA cases within ~30 months involving alleged kickbacks/improper remuneration to referring physicians is a behavioral pattern.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A confirms a second, post-cutoff-development-relevant FCA case in active litigation. Mode B: the framework's anti-kickback / referral-pattern detector flags MYGN as a repeat actor in this exact compliance lane. The 10-K's risk-factor language about 'private individuals' bringing qui tam suits — read against the actual ledger of two qui tam suits in three years — is the type of euphemism the framework is designed to surface. Even if Carolina Urology is ultimately dismissed, the recidivism alone deserves a discount, and the served complaint is a 2026 cash-and-attention drain on top of the UHC and refi cliffs.

rfm_tuples.R: The Company has only one payor that accounted for more than 10% of accounts receivable at December 31, 2024 and 2023. The balance of accounts receivable from the payor represented 18% and 12% of the total accounts receivable balance as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively. [Medicare is] approximately 12%, 12%, and 14% of total revenue for the years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022.
rfm_tuples.f: Reconcile the rising A/R concentration (12% -> 18% of total A/R at one payor) against the simultaneous UHC coverage termination. If UHC is the 18%-of-A/R payor, the receivables aging is the leading edge of a collectibility risk that the 10-K does not link.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Note 12 Concentrations + Critical Audit Matter on revenue measurement
rfm_tuples.M_value: Top-payor A/R concentration rose from 12% (12/31/2023) to 18% (12/31/2024) — a 50% relative jump in 12 months. The 10-K does NOT name this payor. Medicare is disclosed as 12% of revenue (not A/R). EY's critical audit matter is the measurement of revenue — specifically 'changes in payor mix, historical and current payment trends and other changes in payor behavior.' If UHC is the 18% A/R name (plausible given UHC was paying for $45M of GeneSight plus other tests), the post-1/1/2025 cancellation creates significant collectibility risk on the December-quarter receivable.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the 10-K discloses A/R concentration without naming the payor, but the framework can connect (a) the 50% relative jump in single-payor A/R, (b) the UHC GeneSight cancellation, and (c) EY's critical audit matter on revenue measurement. If the 18% A/R payor is UHC, then 18% of $121.2M = ~$21.8M of trade receivable is exposed to a payor that is winding down a relationship — a separately disclosed reserve risk.

rfm_tuples.R: Legal settlements decreased by $134.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024 compared to the prior year. In the prior year, we incurred $112.8 million for legal settlements, including $77.5 million related to the securities class action settlement and $34.0 million in connection with the Ravgen settlement. As part of the Ravgen settlement, we agreed to pay Ravgen $21.3 million if it successfully concluded in its favor all of Ravgen's litigations and... [2024 legal settlements were $(21.3)M income — i.e., reversal of the Ravgen contingent payable].
rfm_tuples.f: Decompose the FY24 operating loss to test whether the GAAP-improvement narrative is operationally real or one-time-driven. FY23 had $112.8M of legal expense; FY24 had a $21.3M legal credit (reversal of the Ravgen contingent). That is a $134M YoY swing in a single non-operating line.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 7 MD&A — Operating Expenses bridge + Note 12
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 operating loss $(123.5)M vs FY23 $(257.4)M. Of the $134M YoY improvement, $134.1M came from the legal-settlements line (Ravgen contingent reversal of $21.3M plus the FY23 base of $112.8M not recurring). After backing out legal settlements (and the $56.8M FY24 impairment vs $0 in FY23), the underlying YoY operating performance is roughly flat to modestly worse — masked by the legal accounting. Stock-based compensation $49.8M is 6% of revenue. Operating cash use $(8.7)M in FY24 was much better than the $(110.9)M FY23 figure, but FY23 was also distorted by the cash legal settlements paid out.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the 10-K narrates FY24 as a turnaround year ('revenue +11%, operating loss cut in half'), but the operating-loss improvement is almost entirely the absence of a prior-year legal settlement and a $21.3M contingent reversal. The lying-by-framing pattern: improvement attributable to one-time accounting items presented inside a narrative of operating progress.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Ernst & Young LLP since 2006 (19-year tenure). Big 4. PCAOB ID 42. Unqualified opinion on financial statements; unqualified opinion on ICFR. No Item 4.01 8-K events. One CAM (measurement of revenue / payor estimation). No going-concern paragraph.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Auditor history is genuinely clean — Mode A deterministic scanners (which the framework runs first) correctly return CLEAN_BIG4_TENURE, so the discrimination must come from Mode B. A 19-year tenure on a serially loss-making molecular diagnostics company is a long tenure, but there is no signal of audit-firm friction. The single CAM (revenue measurement) is the same area Mode A flagged as the highest-judgment lever and is consistent with the UHC payor-mix risk.

rfm_tuples.R: [KPMG-style 'we believe' liquidity language plus] Approximately 63% of our revenue comes from private third-party payors. [And:] The transition of our senior leadership team or the loss of any member of our senior management team may create uncertainty, involve a diversion of resources and management attention, or cause us to experience difficulties in competing effectively, developing our tests and implementing our business strategies. [Plus single-segment reporting]
rfm_tuples.f: Test whether the segment-reporting structure is being used to mask product-level pressure. The 10-K reports a single operating segment but four product categories (Hereditary Cancer, Tumor Profiling, Prenatal, Pharmacogenomics). The Q1 10-Q confirms three of four categories had revenue declines or per-test price declines.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q1 2025 10-Q Note 13 Segment Reporting + revenue category table
rfm_tuples.M_value: Single-segment reporting (CODM is CEO; only consolidated net loss is measured). Q1 2025 product category result: Hereditary Cancer rev -2% (price -5%, vol +3%); Tumor Profiling rev -5% (vol -14%); Prenatal rev +11% (the only mover); Pharmacogenomics rev -20% (vol +2%, price -22%). 3 of 4 product categories are deteriorating on revenue and on price-per-test. The single-segment structure means there is no segment-level operating-income disclosure to test against — but Prenatal alone is roughly 25% of revenue and is the only positive contributor.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: the single-segment structure prevents an investor from confirming whether the Prenatal franchise is funding the rest of the company. The 10-K's narrative is portfolio-balanced, but the actual mix is concentrating into one product (Foresight prenatal screening) just as three others (Hereditary, Tumor, GeneSight) are simultaneously losing ground. This is the structural setup that leads to a future write-down on whichever of the three deteriorating product groups holds the remaining intangibles.

rfm_tuples.R: The resulting fair value of the Pharmacogenomics reporting unit exceeded its carrying value by 43.6%. [...] discount rate reflective of the risk-adjusted cost of capital of 10.0%. [Impairment of GeneSight developed-technology asset $43.0M; Pharmacogenomics goodwill not yet written off.]
rfm_tuples.f: Pressure-test the Pharmacogenomics impairment cushion against the actual Q1 2025 outcome. A 10.0% WACC implies a low-cost-of-capital assumption for a company with deteriorating EBITDA, an ABL maturing in 14 months, and a goodwill-bearing reporting unit that just lost its largest commercial payor. A 22% Q1 price miss on a 43.6% cushion is mathematically thin.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Critical Accounting Estimates — Goodwill + Q1 2025 10-Q revenue per test
rfm_tuples.M_value: Pharmacogenomics reporting unit cushion: 43.6% over carrying value at 12/31/2024 (post-$43M GeneSight intangible writedown). WACC assumed: 10.0%. Actual Q1 2025 Pharmacogenomics revenue per test: -22% YoY (vs an implicit DCF base case of stabilization). If the DCF base case assumed flat-to-modestly-down 2025 revenue, a -20% revenue start to the year compresses the present-value cushion materially. A second impairment in 2025 of Pharmacogenomics goodwill is plausible and not disclosed as a near-term risk in the 10-K.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: management ran the impairment test with a 10.0% WACC and modeled a 43.6% cushion. The Q1 10-Q shows the actual Q1 was worse than the DCF base case implies — so the cushion is already eroding 90 days post-test. The 10-K does not say 'if Q1 2025 comes in at -20% revenue, we will need to impair the Pharmacogenomics reporting unit further' — which is the kind of forward-looking sensitivity that the framework's claim-evolution detector targets.

summary: MYGN is a high-conviction Mode-B-heavy SHORT-tier detection. Deterministic scanners return NO_GOING_CONCERN and CLEAN_BIG4_TENURE (EY since 2006), so a Mode-A-only framework would mis-score this as benign. The Mode B cluster, however, is dense and entirely sourced from inside the 10-K and the pre-cutoff Q1 2025 10-Q. (1) The UnitedHealthcare GeneSight coverage cancellation eliminates $45M of FY24 revenue and triggered a $43M intangible impairment, but the residual Pharmacogenomics reporting unit cushion is only 43.6% on a 10.0% WACC — and the Q1 2025 10-Q shows the price-per-test outcome was -22%, materially worse than any reasonable DCF base case, setting up a likely 2025 second impairment. (2) The Hereditary Cancer franchise (44% of revenue) silently rolled over: FY24 +6% price became Q1 2025 -5% price, a reversal the 10-K does not flag and the 10-Q does not explain — a textbook claim-evolution tell. (3) Liquidity: cash fell from $102.4M to $91.8M and ABL borrowings rose from $39.6M to $59.3M in a single quarter; availability collapsed from $56M to $42M; ABL matures 6/30/2026, inside the post-cutoff window, against a deteriorating revenue trajectory. (4) Capital allocation: no share repurchases, but a CSO 10b5-1 plan adopted 12/12/2024 (post-UHC announcement). (5) Governance: CEO Paul Diaz announced his departure 2/24/2025, four days before signing the 10-K, with a one-year consulting tail; new CEO is a 16-month-tenured internal COO; the CCO seat is open. (6) Legal recidivism: a second FCA qui tam (Carolina Urology Partners) was filed within 5 months of MYGN's $48M Crescendo Bioscience FCA settlement; the new case was unsealed 1/22/2025 and served 4/16/2025. (7) FY24 operating loss improvement of $134M is almost entirely the absence of FY23's $112.8M legal-settlements expense plus a $21.3M Ravgen contingent reversal — underlying operating performance is flat to modestly worse. The framework's correct verdict: MYGN was not lying about distress in a forward-looking-statement sense (no going-concern), but was framing a stack of structurally bad news (UHC cliff, hereditary cancer pricing reversal, refi cliff, leadership turnover, recidivist FCA exposure) as a turnaround narrative. Composite should be SEVERE.
